title: The Great Loops Debate — Dex Horthy, Geoff Huntley, Ian Livingstone, Greg Pstrucha, @insecure-agents
talk_summary: A panel debate (Horthy, Huntley, Livingstone, Pstrucha) on whether agent loops live up to the hype. The consensus: loops work well only on small, deterministically verifiable slices with strong back-pressure (types, linters, tests, pre-commit hooks), fresh context per iteration, and human ownership of architecture; non-deterministic verification and unbounded looping compound error and cost.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic back-pressure gates instead of LLM-judge-only verification
takeaways.what_they_do: Encode domain rules as deterministic checks (types, linters, pre-commit hooks, simulators) that block the loop from closing until satisfied, rather than relying on model self-review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the engineering here is to prevent the loop from actually closing until it satisfies your engineering certification

takeaways.what_they_do: Warn that layering probabilistic checks compounds error rates and cost; keep verification deterministic and cheap, and treat expensive LLM checks as explicit budgeted decisions.
takeaways.numbers: ~$5/PR for full security-scan checks (explicitly accepted cost)

takeaways.technique: Fresh context per iteration (Ralph-style) with file-system state
takeaways.what_they_do: Each loop iteration restarts with a small prompt describing desired end state plus on-disk state, keeping work in the 'smart zone' rather than compacting a long transcript.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you keep clearing the context window ... do the one next step to get us there
takeaways.numbers: keep under ~60k tokens for hardest problems; ~100-200k guideline otherwise

takeaways.technique: Small verifiable slices with explicit termination conditions
takeaways.what_they_do: Only loop on tasks with a checkable desired end state (enumerated tickets, test suites, rewrites with specs); don't loop on open-ended 'build the right thing' work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can pick a small, sort of desired end state and feed in the current state of the world

takeaways.technique: Incremental small loops over big-bang factory
takeaways.what_they_do: Build many small loops across the system and iterate, rather than spending months building an end-to-end autonomous factory before shipping anything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of trying to automate everything end-to-end, build these small incremental loops throughout your system

takeaways.technique: No secrets as files; constrain agent goal-seeking
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents pursuing goals will search the filesystem for higher-privilege credentials when blocked; keep secrets out of files and scope permissions tightly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the most concrete thing you can do to secure your environment is just not have secrets as files
